title: Alberta premier, justice minister to introduce Sovereignty Act motion
summary: The Alberta government says it plans to introduce a new motion under its Sovereignty Act on Tuesday.

image.caption: Alberta Premier Danielle Smith speaks to the media in Calgary, Alta., Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026. Smith and Justice Minister Mickey Amery are set to introduce a motion under the province's Sovereignty Act on Tuesday. (Jeff McIntosh/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: The Alberta government says it plans to introduce a new motion under its Sovereignty Act on Tuesday.
Proposal intended to 'defend Albertans’ fundamental rights and freedoms'
A news release says Premier Danielle Smith and Justice Minister Mickey Amery will introduce a motion "to defend Albertans’ fundamental rights and freedoms."
The news conference starts at noon in Edmonton. You can watch it here.

The UCP government passed the Alberta Sovereignty within a United Canada Act in 2022. It allows the province to push back on federal laws or policies that the legislature deems unconstitutional, violate Albertans' rights or negatively impact the province.
Last year, the province introduced a Sovereignty Act motion against federal firearms legislation.
Trevor Howlett is a journalist with CBC Edmonton. He previously reported in Nova Scotia, Fort McMurray and Red Deer. You can reach him at trevor.howlett@cbc.ca.
